forgot to put this in my garden update, but i threw some pulverized lime (prob about a palmful around each plant) on my maters, and it seems to have corrected the blossom end rot!

Yay!

Wasnt getting any maters that were turning yellow or red without rot, and after the lime and a good rain, ive pulled at least 3 or 4 that were pretty red, with less splotchy areas, and NO ROT :)

Just throwing this out there for fellow voaters who may be experiencing the same thing. I tried the calcium spray, but it did not work. I did throw a proper application of pelletized lime into the dirt before ever planting the garden, but still got the rot. After applying the powdered lime to already established plants, which were already bearing fruit, it seems to have worked.
I was always told end rot was a result of inconsistent watering. I noticed I will have some plants lose their first few tomatoes to rot, then produce well later that year.

good to hear another idea on this. maybe theres a bit of placebo effect going on here.

i havent watered the garden yet this year. round here, summers are hot as balls, with thunderstorms about every other day seems like...

every time i move the top inch of dirt, the dirt under it is still moist. i would actually have lilked less frequent rain, but deeper watering, to stimulate deeper roots.
